### instance-store-attach-only-at-launch

### instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop

**Claim.** Data on an instance store volume persists when the instance is rebooted, but not when the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated; then every block of the volume is cryptographically erased.

### instance-store-first-write-slower-initialize

**Claim.** On some instance store volumes the first write to each location is slower than later writes, so AWS recommends initializing the drives for high disk performance; instance types with direct-attached SSD and TRIM support give maximum performance at launch without initialization.

**Write it as.** `performs more slowly than subsequent writes` · `maximum performance at launch time, without initialization`

**Scope.** some instance store volumes; not needed on SSD instance store with TRIM support.

> "Because of the way that Amazon EC2 virtualizes disks, the first write to any location on some instance store volumes performs more slowly than subsequent writes."
> — [Initialize instance store volumes on EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/disk-performance.html)

> "Instance types with direct-attached solid state drives (SSD) and TRIM support provide maximum performance at launch time, without initialization."
> — [Initialize instance store volumes on EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/disk-performance.html)

> "However, if you require high disk performance, we recommend that you initialize your drives by writing once to every drive location before production use."
> — [Initialize instance store volumes on EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/disk-performance.html)

### instance-store-nvme-encryption-xts-aes-256

**Claim.** Data on NVMe instance storage is encrypted with an XTS-AES-256 block cipher in a hardware module on the instance; the keys are unique per device, destroyed when the instance stops or terminates, and you cannot disable this encryption or supply your own key.

**Write it as.** `XTS-AES-256 block cipher`

**Scope.** per NVMe instance store volume; default; not adjustable; always on; cannot be disabled.

> "The data on NVMe instance storage is encrypted using an XTS-AES-256 block cipher implemented in a hardware module on the instance. The encryption keys are generated using the hardware module and are unique to each NVMe instance storage device. All encryption keys are destroyed when the instance is stopped or terminated and cannot be recovered. You cannot disable this encryption and you cannot provide your own encryption key."
> — [SSD instance store volumes for EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ssd-instance-store.html)
